name: Mice and the Ogre
notes: Brandon's emergent-sequence example (FR-18): the players start screaming, so mice rush the room — a fake minor encounter, really just running by and biting on their way down the hall, because the noise woke a huge ogre. Five rounds later the ogre arrives, roars, smashes the wall, and the lights go out. Validate with `bun run cutscene --file examples/mice-ogre.json --validate-only` — no connection needed. To play it, the Mouse and Ogre actors must exist in the world, combat must be running (the waitRound step waits on the live round clock), and the rubble tile must be uploaded to worlds/testbed/rubble.png (uploadTilePack covers the whole pack). The room is the Lich's Lair Entry Hall (1600x1600, south door at (800,1500), far door at (800,100), party around the center (800,800)). The bite rolls post visibly in chat (showInChat); applying the rolled damage to HP is the GM's call — the sequence runner has no variable passing, so a rolled amount cannot feed a damage step in the same expansion.

steps.content: The shouting echoes down the hall — and something answers. A tide of mice pours through the south door, squeaking, biting, scrambling for the far hall.
The ogre ROARS — and brings both fists down on the south wall.
The torches gutter and die. The room goes dark — and something huge is breathing in it.
